intro: Dealing with blocked drains & toilets in Kerobokan & Umalas usually comes down to two things: steady family use wearing out older pipework, or the high water table after monsoon pushing pressure back into your septic system. We clear toilets, sinks, showers and sewer lines with a proper drain snake rather than chemical plungers that corrode joints and poison tank bacteria. A quick photo or ten-second clip on WhatsApp is all we need to tell you what's going on and quote the job.

sections.h3: Why Villas Here Clog Up More Often
sections.text: Families living full-time in Kerobokan Kelod or Batu Belig put continuous load on heaters, pumps and septic tanks — far more than a short-stay guest ever would. Add the rice-field water table sitting close to the surface, and every heavy downpour pushes groundwater against your drain lines from below. Older villas sharing streets with new builds means both corroded iron pipes and fresh PVC joints showing up within fifty metres of each other. That mix makes blockages here less about one big mistake and more about gradual pressure building over months.

sections.h3: What We Actually Clear Day to Day
sections.text: The calls we see most from Umalas and surrounding lanes are a toilet that backs up after two flushes, a shower drain slowing week by week, a sewer line reeking of rotting organic matter even when nothing is running, and a sink trap finally giving out under years of hair and soap scum. In every case we work with a flexible drain snake to pull the obstruction free mechanically. No caustic powders, no pour-and-pray bottles — just physical removal so the beneficial bacteria in your septic tank stay intact.

sections.h3: Send Us a Photo Before You Panic
sections.text: Open WhatsApp, point your phone at the affected fixture or the access point where water is backing up, and send a short clip if you can. Tell us which area you're in — Kerobokan Kelod, Umalas, Batu Belig — and whether it's one bathroom or the whole villa slowing down. From those details we'll tell you on the spot whether it's a simple trap clear-out or something deeper in the line, and what the job costs. No obligation, no call charges, just a straight quote based on what you show us.

sections.h3: Keeping Your Drains Clear Between Visits
sections.text: Because groundwater here stays high year-round, flush each toilet once every couple of days even when nobody's home; stagnant water in the trap invites root intrusion from nearby garden trees. Keep hair out of shower drains with a simple catch net rather than reaching for chemical unblockers that wipe out the bacteria your tank depends on. If the drain smell creeps back after a monsoon week, treat that as your cue to book a quick snake-through before it hardens into a full blockage.

faq.q: Do you use chemicals to unblock toilets?
faq.a: No. We work with a mechanical drain snake so nothing harsh enters your pipes or septic tank. Chemicals may give temporary relief but they corrode joints and kill the bacteria your tank relies on to break down waste.

faq.q: How do I get a price without calling anyone?
faq.a: Send a photo or short video of the problem on WhatsApp along with your neighbourhood name. We reply with an honest assessment and a quote based on what we see — no phone call needed at any point.

faq.q: Why does my drain smell worse right after rain?
faq.a: Kerobokan and Umalas sit above a high water table, so heavy rain pushes groundwater against your drain lines and can force odour back up through traps. A routine snake-through after the wet season keeps those lines clear and the smell under control.
